subject.title: [Bug] Docker sandbox container name collision across multiple instances on same host

question: Should OpenClaw accept workspace-scoped non-shared sandbox runtime identity, including the one-time reset of existing non-shared Docker/browser/SSH sandbox runtimes, as the fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug is source-proven and security-sensitive, but the best fix changes the persistent sandbox identity contract and therefore needs maintainer acceptance of the upgrade and cleanup behavior.

options.title: Accept workspace-scoped identity
options.body: Refresh and land the active candidate PR or equivalent so non-shared sandbox runtimes are keyed by resolved workspace and old non-shared runtimes are recreated once.

options.title: Require a migration first
options.body: Pause the candidate fix until a doctor or migration path preserves or explicitly cleans up old non-shared runtime state before changing identity.

options.title: Split backend policy
options.body: Separate Docker, browser, SSH, and local workspace identity decisions if maintainers do not want all non-shared sandbox surfaces to move together.

recommendation.title: Accept workspace-scoped identity
recommendation.body: Refresh and land the active candidate PR or equivalent so non-shared sandbox runtimes are keyed by resolved workspace and old non-shared runtimes are recreated once.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sandbox feature-history signal and is the best available owner for the compatibility/security direction choice.
